News.title: Americans warned after urgent travel warning issued to popular European country with pristine Mediterranean views
News.content:
AMERICANS have been warned to remain vigilant while visiting a European country famous for its jaw-dropping Mediterranean views.

They need to exercise extreme caution due to the long arm of Iran’s Supreme Leader.





The US Embassy in Albania has warned American citizens of threats connected to the Tehran regime.

Iran-linked groups could target Americans and US-affiliated entities in Albania, the Tirana-based embassy’s alert said.

This includes while visiting tourist hotspots, restaurants and even shopping.

“Groups associated with Iran may seek to target entities associated with the US or Iranian opposition elements in Albania,” it explained.



“They may also target common venues, such as tourist sites, shopping malls, hotels, clubs, and restaurants.

“We encourage American citizens to exercise increased vigilance.”

Travelers concerned about their security in Albania were advised to monitor local media for updates, and to be aware of their surroundings.

American citizens should double-check their personal security plans and keep cell phones charged in case of emergency, it was also recommended.



Bajram Begaj, Albania’s president, said in early April that he was in daily contact with the National Security Council, which has been monitoring the potential threat.

He was being “informed about every situation and scenario, as well as all measures taken under security protocols,” the presidency added in a statement.

“The President of the Republic continues to communicate with the institutions responsible for public and national security, which are in constant coordination and collaboration with our partners.”

The embassy’s warning comes as experts continue to warn of Iran’s increased use of hybrid threats.

These include cyberattacks, and sabotage, reported the Center for Strategic and International Studies on April 9.



Donald Trump has indicated that peace negotiations with Iran’s leaders could resume this week.

He has also told Fox Business the war was “very close to being over”.

News.title: Tourist on honeymoon fighting for life after being attacked by shark with his leg ‘stripped of flesh’
News.content:
BEAST STRIKES Tourist on honeymoon fighting for life after being attacked by shark with his leg ‘stripped of flesh’

A MAN is fighting for his life after losing his leg to a shark attack on his honeymoon at a Brit holiday hotspot.

The Spanish newlywed suffered extreme blood loss when his leg was “stripped of flesh” after he was attacked by the vicious beast while swimming.



He had to have his leg amputated after being airlifted to hospital.



A family member of his wife told El Periodico Mediterraneo: “With one bite, it took all the flesh from the knee down off her husband’s leg.”

Another close friend said: “They are trying to save him, he’s in intensive care, but the medical conditions there are very precarious.”

Local news reports say the man hailed from Alicante and just gotten married.

The pair headed to the Indian Ocean paradise for their first holiday together as man and wife.



The horror incident is understood to have happened on Monday afternoon off Kooddoo, one of the inhabitated islands of Gaafu Alif Atoll.

The victim was reportedly part of a group that entered the water at a popular site near the Kooddoo fish processing plant, a location known for high shark activity.

It’s understood the man was rushed to the Ga. Atoll Hospital before being airlifted to Male, the densely-populated capital of the Maldives.

He was then admitted to an intensive care unit at ADK Hospital.

News.title: Terminally ill OAP, 81, jailed for tying up 95-year-old woman in attempted robbery to help pay for his own funeral
News.content:
RAID PLOT Terminally ill OAP, 81, jailed for tying up 95-year-old woman in attempted robbery to help pay for his own funeral

A TERMINALLY ill pensioner has been jailed after he tied up a 95-year-old woman and demanded cash to pay for his own funeral.

Edwin Morrison, 81, targeted Mary Morgan because she used to tip him the “princely sum” of £2 when he dropped off medication in his former job as a pharmacy courier.



He had been diagnosed with incurable kidney cancer in summer 2024 and told he would probably have less than two years to live.



Keen not to have his family pay for his funeral, Morrison hatched the robbery plot.

He tied Mary up in her home in Salford, Greater Manchester, with cable ties and shouted “give me your money“.

The pensioner pleaded with him to let her go and said she could not breathe as Morrison strangled her but he just told her to “shut up”.

Morrison then fled the property empty-handed after Mary’s mobile hairdresser arrived.



He has now been jailed for seven years after he pleaded guilty to attempted robbery.

Judge Peter Horgan said it was “very likely” Morrison would die in custody.

He added: “Your motivation to act in this way was utterly self-centred and without thought for the impact on anybody else.”

Manchester Crown Court heard Morrison had set up an online GoFundMe appeal titled “Help to bury me” as he outlined his health problems.



He wrote: “More or less been told to go in a corner and see my time out. I have no money to cover funeral costs and other incidentals.”

But prosecutors said Morrison was regularly gambling at his local bookies in the months before the attack.

He was also said to have expressed “concerns” about funding a new kitchen at the home where he lived with his then long-term partner.

On January 27, he tricked his way into Mary’s home by claiming he wanted to discuss the new bin collection date.

Once inside, Morrison bound her hands together while demanding cash.



He also put his hand around her throat and repeatedly asked for the woman’s money and purse.

After he was interrupted by the hairdresser, Morrison held his hands up as if he was going to grab her throat too before he fled empty-handed.

Detective Inspector Paul Davies, of Greater Mancheser Police, said: “It was a terrifying ordeal for the victim and Morrison’s actions of targeting a woman in her own home were shocking.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Her resilience and strength following this vile crime have been truly inspirational and I am glad that the investigative team have been able to get her the justice she deserves.

“I also want to commend the brave actions of her hairdresser who arrived as the crime was happening. She prevented Morrison from doing anything further, got him out of the living room and called 999 straight away.”

News.title: Are the ‘Rolex Rippers’ back? How thieves who assault men to steal watches could be prowling streets again
News.content:
CRIME WATCH Are the ‘Rolex Rippers’ back? How thieves who assault men to steal watches could be prowling streets again

FEARS have been raised over the return of a female Rolex ripper gang, as mystery distraction thieves allegedly rob and sexually assault two men.

Cops are probing two “linked” incidents of pensioners being robbed by unidentified women while walking in Aylesbury, Buckinghamshire.





Both of the robberies happened within days of one another in Aylesbury with both suspects using the same tactics.

The methods employed in the recent robberies have previously been used by a notorious gang of watch thieves.

Thames Valley Police (TVP) has since confirmed it is treating the two Aylesbury incidents as linked.

TVP is also liaising with other forces and “keeping an open mind” as to whether there are links between the Aylesbury robberies and other similar cases.

The crimes have seen the return of the tactics used in a spate of thefts carried out by an all-female gang in the south of England in 2021.

Only one member of the notorious all-female Rolex ripper gang, which played a part in some 15 successful robberies, was ever caught.

The group of crooks used distraction techniques before attempting to touch or “cuddle” their victims while nabbing the valuable timepieces from their wrists.

Stefania Tinica, a Romanian national, was the only member of the group to be caught by cops.



She was taken into custody at Luton Airport as she tried to flee the UK in 2022.

Tinica was jailed for 40 months over her role in a theft in Poole, Dorset and a failed robbery some months earlier in Cheshire.

The theft in Poole saw a £15,930 Rolex Submariner timepiece stolen from a pensioner – the valuable watch was never recovered.

The organised crime gang is believed by cops to be made up of mostly Eastern European women.

They struck in Dorset, Hampshire, West Sussex, Surrey, Gloucestershire and Cheshire.



Most of the cases involved older men targeted by younger women with the same tactics being used in each.

Two new incidents with almost identical circumstances have now been reported to police in Aylesbury, Buckinghamshire.

The first victim was attacked on a footpath between Jackson Road and Aston Close just after midday on March 19.



Police say he was approached by a woman who touched him inappropriately over his clothing.

Cops said the attacker then snatched a gold Cubin Link chain from the OAP’s neck, before making off with the jewellery.

The suspect is described as being aged in her early to mid-thirties and around 5ft to 5ft 2ins tall.

She is thought to be Malaysian or Thai in appearance, with an accent – she had her hair tied up at the time of the attack.

Days later, on April 8, another unsuspecting OAP had been walking in Richmond Road when he was approached at around 12:45pm.



The second victim was also touched inappropriately above his clothes and had a Rolex watch stolen from his wrist.

According to the police description, the attacker is a white woman, aged in her twenties or thirties, with long dark hair.

The woman is described as being roughly 5ft tall with a Spanish accent.

In both of the chilling new attacks the victims were offered sexual services before allegedly being sexually assaulted and robbed.

It is not known if there is any link between the recent spate of attacks and those carried out by the all female Rolex ripper gang in 2021.



TVP investigating officer Detective Constable Mandy Cutler said: “This incident has occurred in the middle of the afternoon in Aylesbury.

“(It) has very similar circumstances to a similar incident which occurred last week on 8 April.

“At this stage, I am treating these incidents as linked to each other.

“I am also keeping an open mind as to whether these two incidents are linked to a wider issue of similar such incidents occurring elsewhere in the country.

“We are liaising with partner forces to ascertain whether there are any discernible links to these offences.



“I would urge anybody who has any information or concerns to please get in touch with us.

“You will be listened to and supported, and any information, no matter how significant this may seem, may be crucial in assisting this investigation.”

Separately, TVP told The Sun the force was pursuing the possibility that the thefts were linked to other possible cases.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A spokesperson said: “It’s very early stages in our investigations, but it is a line of enquiry that our officers are following; although at this stage, there is nothing definitively that can confirm any links.

“The methods used in the two cases in Aylesbury are being treated as linked due to similar modus operandis, and as such, an open mind is being kept on possible wider links, but at this early stage it is not possible to confirm or deny these links.”

News.title: Dark rise of manosphere influencer Clavicular who preaches about using meth for weight loss to lonely male disciples
News.content:
HE’S the poster boy for the disturbing social media ‘looksmaxxing’ community, where men try to perfect their physical attractiveness in a bid to increase their chances with women.

But now, following a string of recent scandals, manosphere influencer Clavicular has been rushed to hospital in Miami following a suspected overdose.





The social media star, whose real name is Braden Peters, had been live-streaming on the website Kick on Tuesday when the broadcast suddenly ended.

Fans had been concerned after the streamer appeared to be slurring his words, and was later seen slumping in his chair before his friends quickly called an ambulance.

He was said to be in a stable condition in hospital.



But this isn’t the first time Clavicular – who was recently grilled by Louis Theroux in the Netflix documentary Inside The Manosphere – has caused controversy with his extreme and worrying behaviour.

The 20-year-old content creator thrives off notoriety and shock, proffering dangerous advice to his followers from smashing their bones with a hammer to achieve a better jawline – known by some looksmaxxers as a $5 beauty tip – to taking crystal meth to suppress appetite.

While his life now is one of extremes, he claims to have had a normal childhood growing up in New Jersey, with a businessman father, stay-at-home mother, little sister, family dog, winter ski holidays and summers at the beach.

But when he fixated on something, as he has explained in interviews, it became an obsession.



That obsessive personality trait became more sinister when teenage Peters hit the gym and it changed the course of his life.

He started working out, studying body composition intently online and trawling bodybuilding forums before landing on a website about looksmaxxing.

He renamed himself Clavicular — after the clavicle — and soon professed to have worked out a magic formula to transcend the ranks of other teenage boys desperate for female adulation.

His views appear rooted in the toxic manosphere ‘blackpill’ ideology that men’s success with women is almost exclusively down to genetics and only men who look a certain way can win the affections of the ‘top tier’ of women, who are reduced to mere sex objects and status symbols.

TikTok became his 21st century fairground freak show, where his bizarre and increasingly concerning antics gained millions of views.



And as his fanbase grew, Clavicular took the reckless looksmaxxing trend further than anyone else.

He’s spoken about becoming the ‘lab rat of the community,’ the guy willing to risk everything to ‘ascend’ – which is looksmaxxing speak for having a major, if questionable, glow-up.

Peters claims he began injecting testosterone at the age of 14, bought off the internet with no medical or parental guidance.



He now says his body can’t produce it naturally and believes he is currently infertile.

BBC documentary maker James Blake studied young men like Clavicular for his film, Men of the Manosphere. He says while a lot of their behaviour comes from similar experiences, Clavicular has pushed it to the next level.

“What stood out is that a lot of it stems from the same place, insecurity, identity, and a desire to feel in control,” James tells The Sun.

“With Clavicular, what you’re seeing is that pushed to an extreme. Creators like him operate in an environment where the more shocking the behaviour, the more attention it gets due to how social media algorithms work, so there’s a constant pressure on him to escalate.

“More attention means more opportunities to monetise that audience.



“That can lead to dangerous territory, where even self-destructive acts such as Clavicular advising young men hit their own faces with a hammer to shape their jawline or advising to take crystal meth to stay lean is reframed as discipline or part of self-improvement.”

As twisted as this lifestyle might seem, it is a lucrative one. Clavicular has amassed millions of followers on social media and claims to earn around £75,000 a month from Kick.

And for a fee, he claims he can also coach other people to ‘ascend’ to his self-proclaimed levels of physical perfection.

He has also become prolific at ‘clipfarming’, where the things he livestreams are so twisted that they become viral clips.



What is looksmaxxing? A DISTURBING trend is urging young men to take extreme measures to improve their looks – all so they can get a girlfriend. From smashing their own faces with a hammer to chisel a better jawline to having leg extension surgery to be taller, experts fear the twisted craze of looksmaxxing could turn deadly – and also harm young women. First emerging in the early 2010s, looksmaxxing was a phrase used on disturbing misogynistic online forums. The term quickly spiralled from self-improvement to a desperate desire for teenage boys to fit in by undergoing life-altering and permanent surgery. In the last few years, it has spiked in popularity on social media platforms – with users widely sharing stories of how they got their “good looks”. The basic principle is to improve your looks to help attract love interests – and a draconian spin-off has now emerged known as “hardmaxxing”. Hardmaxxing comes from warped forums which recommend extreme measures to help others become “more attractive”, from Botox injections and steroids to expensive surgery. These forums are also being blamed for a worrying number of suicides among young men who feel they don’t look attractive enough, an expert told The Sun. Michael Halpin, Associate Professor of Sociology at Dalhousie University, said: “I observed a teenager stating that he was going to take his own life if he did not reach 6ft in height. “While other users were told they were too ugly for ‘looksmaxxing’ and they should consider suicide. “They are told they need to looksmax if they want to look better or ‘normal.’” Read more here.

But his controversy extends much further than how far he is willing to push his body and risk his own health in pursuit of perceived perfection.

On Christmas Eve he was temporarily banned from the Kick platform after appearing to run over a person while driving a Tesla Cybertruck.

He was then heard saying: “Is he dead? Hopefully.”

He has also publicly aligned with the world’s most notorious manosphere figures, Andrew Tate and Nick Fuentes, partying with them at a Miami nightclub as the group shamefully sang along to Kanye West’s antisemitic song “Heil Hitler”.



He also caused outrage when he live-streamed himself apparently injecting his then 17-year-old girlfriend with fat-dissolving peptides to reshape her jaw.

And earlier this month he was arrested and hit with a misdemeanour charge for allegedly instigating a catfight between his current girlfriend and another female influencer — which he livestreamed.

Peters’ girlfriend, 24-year-old Violent Lentz, was captured on video fighting with a 19-year-old influencer while their group was staying at an Airbnb.

In a separate incident, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission announced it was launching an investigation after a video appearing to show Clavicular firing a gun at an alligator went viral.

James Blake believes that content like this can blur the lines for impressionable young followers as to what is ‘normal’ and what is completely unhinged.



He explains: “Many of the followers and members of these communities are extremely young, impressionable and for the most part lost as they are still finding their identity and way in life.

“When young men and boys are exposed to this kind of content repeatedly, it can start to blur the line between what’s extreme and what feels acceptable or even aspirational.

“At the core, most of the audience aren’t extreme themselves, they’re often looking for direction or confidence, which means they are entering into this world already very impressionable and dare I say exploitable.”



But despite Clavicular’s willingness to spout dangerous advice online and make demeaning comments about women to his fans, it seems he doesn’t like being questioned about it.

This week he stormed out of an interview with 60 Minutes Australia after being asked if he was an incel.

“I mean, how could you ask me that question as a follow-up after you asked me about my relationships to women?” he frostily replied. “I mean, that’s quite literally the worst sequence of questions I think I’ve ever heard.”

Interviewer Adam Hegarty then rephrased the question: “Looksmaxxing was obviously a term created by the incel community. How do you feel about being linked to that group?”

“I’m not linked to that group in any way,” replied Clavicular. “Looksmaxxing is self-improvement, right? So it’s about potentially even ascending out of that category. So that would be kind of one of the goals — to dissociate from being an incel and overcome that. So that doesn’t make sense.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

When Hegarty then questioned why he hung out with the likes of Andrew Tate, Clavicular got defensive, took off his microphone and walked out.

After his latest viral video, where he appeared to put his health on the line once again, critics and fans alike are now questioning how much further he can go in the pursuit of fame and his idea of perfection.

News.title: Tragic influencer’s partner speaking with cops after creepy timeline emerges in her ‘mystery’ Zanzibar death
News.content:
INVESTIGATION TWIST Tragic influencer’s partner speaking with cops after creepy timeline emerges in her ‘mystery’ Zanzibar death

THE fiancé of an American influencer who died during a trip with him on the Tanzanian islands is reportedly speaking with cops in the country.

Joe McCann, 45, is said to be stranded with his passport withheld as investigators in Zanzibar probe the mysterious death of Ashly Robinson, 31.





Robinson was celebrating her 31st birthday with McCann when she was found unconscious in a hotel room on April 8.

She was rushed to the hospital but died the next day from hypoxia caused by strangulation and suffocation, according to local reports.

Authorities have suggested she died by suicide – but her family has stressed they still don’t have final answers and are begging for a clear story from authorities.

They claim McCann didn’t tell them about Robinson’s health issues until 11 hours after it happened – and that he’s been dodging their calls ever since.



The family told the media they didn’t hear about her death until the hotel Robinson was staying at called them.

Now, McCann, who hasn’t made any public comments about his bride to be’s death, is said to be speaking with police, according to the BBC.

“Investigations into the case are ongoing, including awaiting the official medical examination report from doctors,” police reportedly said.

Robinson amassed over 100,000 followers on Instagram by showing off her luxurious lifestyle filled with travel and glamourous fashions.



She had just gotten engaged on the African excursion – and shared a video of McCann getting on one knee in front of a lioness.

“Still taking this in […] somewhere in Africa,” she wrote in the caption.

Robinson’s family said they were baffled over how she could go from celebrating her birthday and a new life with McCann to suddenly dying.

“We are confused about how that could change so drastically,” Robinson’s mom Yolanda Endres told CBS News.

Robinson told her mom she and McCann had gotten into a fight and were staying in different hotel rooms four days before she was found unconscious, Endres told ABC affiliate WPVI.



Zanzibar’s North Unguja police chief Benedict Mapujira confirmed the couple were separated by hotel staff after having a reported disagreement, according to the BBC.

“She was loved. She was not just going to be discarded and forgotten about,” Endres said.

“She’s never done anything that would ever ever lead me to believe that she would do something to harm herself like that. She was happy,” she added.



McCann is the founder of cryptocurrency management firm Asymmetric Financial – which is based in Portland, Oregon.

The U.S. Sun has attempted to reach out to McCann for comment.

If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988, chat on 988lifeline.org, or text Crisis Text Line at 741741.

News.title: North Korea is ‘rapidly’ boosting nuke production at ‘very serious’ rate as nuclear watchdog issues chilling warning
News.content:
NORTH Korea is making “very serious” advances in its ability to produce nuclear weaponry, a top nuclear watchdog has warned.

Under the guidance of dictator Kim Jong Un, the isolated nation is believed to be operating multiple uranium enrichment facilities.





This includes one at the previously decommissioned Yongbyon nuclear site which resumed operations in 2021, according to a South Korean spy report.

These facilities are essential in the production of potentially devastating nuclear warheads.

North Korea is now thought to have approximately 50 warheads at its disposal.

“In our periodic assessments, we have been able to confirm that there’s a rapid increase in operations,” said International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) chief Rafael Grossi.

The agency also noted an increase in operations at Yongbyon’s reprocessing unit and light-water reactor, as well as the activation of other facilities.

“All that points to a very serious increase in the capabilities of [the] DPRK in the area of nuclear weapons production, which is estimated a few dozen warheads,” Grossi said.



The Hermit Kingdom conducted its first nuclear test back in 2006, later cutting off access to IAEA inspectors in 2009.

It is currently the subject of a raft of UN sanctions after previously declaring it will never surrender its nuclear weapons.

Since then, the authoritarian regime is said to have acquired a working nuclear capacity that includes intercontinental ballistic missiles capable of reaching the US mainland.

Agency bosses also noted the worrying construction of a “new facility similar to the enrichment facility in Yongbyon”.

Satellite imagery obtained in April suggests this new building has generators, fuel storage tanks and cooling units.



However, without visiting the site it is “not easy to calculate” any increase in production.

“We consider, looking at the external features of the facility, that there will be a significant increase in the enrichment capacity of the DPRK,” Rossi said.

Asked whether Russia was lending a hand in North Korea’s ongoing nuclear development, Grossi said the IAEA had not seen “anything in particular in that regard.”

Any assistance would build upon the already blossoming relationship between the two anti-western powers.

North Korea has notably sent ground troops and artillery shells to support Vladimir Putin‘s invasion of Ukraine.



Simultaneously, Pyongyang is said to be receiving military technology in return.

Grossi assured South Korea‘s Foreign Minister Cho Hyun that their noisy neighbours’ nuclear activities “remained one of the IAEA’s key issues”.

In return, Cho said Seoul was working to “end hostility and confrontation” with the North Korea in the goal of pursuing peaceful coexistence.

This comes after Kim Jong Un was spotted grinning from ear to ear as he observed missile tests from his new warship on Sunday.

According to the state-run Korean Central New Agency (KCNA), the despot oversaw two strategic cruise missile launches, as well as the launch of three anti-ship missiles from his 5000-ton-class destroyer.



The missiles flew “along the flight orbits set in the sky above the West Sea of Korea and struck the targets with ultra-precision hit accuracy,” the KCNA said.

Unfortunately, one of the destroyers – named Kang Kon – endured a botched launch last year, sparking Kim’s fury.

The naval destroyer ended up on its side after the launch ceremony went drastically wrong.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Satellite images later showed the warship lying on its side beside the launch dock.

However, following repairs, the Kang Kon relaunched in June after being righted using giant balloons.

News.title: Dubai cops ‘access PRIVATE WhatsApp group where vid of Iranian drone damage was shared’ before arresting airline worker
News.content:
DUBAI cops hellbent on locking up dissenters have allegedly been snooping on private WhatsApp messages to sanction arrests.

Police ruthlessly hunted down an Emirati flight attendant who privately shared footage of smoke billowing from the site of an Iranian drone strike in the city.





On feeling his building shake from the impact, the airline worker had decided to record the scary situation and send it to a closed WhatsApp group of colleagues.

But even though the clip was not publicly posted, Dubai‘s digital sniffer dogs were reportedly straight on his case.

According to a police report, the clip was detected through “electronic monitoring operations”.

It is unclear whether the messages were accessed via infiltration or leaked by a member of the group.

But an elite cyber crime unit was allegedly formed to continue gathering evidence in order to identify the culprit.

The unwitting flight attendant was subsequently located, lured to a meeting point and cuffed by police.

He remains in detention after the case was escalated to State Security Prosecution, where charges include publishing information deemed harmful to state interests.



Radha Stirling, CEO of Detained in Dubai, said: “Dubai Police have now explicitly confirmed they are conducting electronic surveillance operations capable of detecting private WhatsApp messages.

“Individuals are being tracked, identified, and arrested not for public statements, but for private exchanges between colleagues.”

Stirling added that a slew of related arrests have dramatically upped the ante on Dubai’s residents and turned the city into a quasi-police state.

She said: “We have just been alerted to a deeply concerning case involving a comedian who has now been detained for nearly a month after performing a one-line sketch.

“He was called into a police station without explanation and has remained in detention for over 28 days under the UAE’s cybercrime laws.



“If this is how the law is being applied, then thousands of expatriates could be at risk, not just for social media posts, but for jokes, satire, or even private messages.”

Stirling has called on global tech platforms to address weaknesses in their security.

She said: “Companies like WhatsApp must answer urgent questions about user privacy.

“If private communications can be detected and used as the basis for arrest by overreaching or hypersensitive states, users worldwide need clarity on how their data is being accessed.”



A Meta spokesperson said: “We protect personal messages with end-to-end encryption using the Signal protocol, which secures your messages before they leave your device.

“This means that no one outside of the chat, not even WhatsApp or Meta, can read, listen to, or share them.”

The Sun has contacted the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs for comment.

The UAE has faced growing accusations of arresting tourists for daring to speak negatively of the country and using kangaroo courts to lock them up.



An eerie handwritten note smuggled out of a hellhole Emirati jail by a Brit prisoner claims that he and 15 others were beaten up by police.

More than 50 Brits have been arrested in Dubai and Abu Dhabi for sharing evidence of drone attacks.

The note shared with The Sun by advocacy group Detained in Dubai was just two lines, but carried a chilling message.

It claimed that the Brit prisoner was beaten by UAE cops and remains locked up without hope of a trial to clear his name.

One line of the note read: “On my case there is 15 people, we all got beaten by the special police force, the case will never go to court.”



It was smuggled out of a UAE jail and passed to Detained in Dubai last month.

It gave details of the packed conditions suffered by those locked up in UAE prisons.

Stirling told the Sun: “A British citizen currently held in the UAE has smuggled out a handwritten note stating that he and fifteen other prisoners in his cell have been beaten by police.”



She highlighted previous cases of UK citizens being beaten up in UAE jails, including Brit grandad Albert Douglas, who was tortured to within an inch of his life in Dubai’s dangerous Al Barsha prison.

She also claimed many of those arrested have bypassed the British Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), because they don’t think it can help them.

Iran has targeted Dubai and Abu Dhabi with hundreds of drones since the start of the Iran war.

Attacks included drone debris causing a huge blaze on the side of the Burj Khalifa and hitting the ritzy Fairmont hotel on the Palm Jumeirah.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Yet as missiles soared through the skies above the cities, Emirati authorities threatened residents with huge fines and jail time for sharing footage of the attacks.

Repressive rules mean anyone sharing or taking photos of Iranian attacks in the UAE could face up to five years behind bars and be fined thousands.

News.title: Young Brit Niaomi Baker stranded 1,000 miles from home after seizure on plane
News.content:
Young Brit Niaomi Baker stranded 1,000 miles from home after seizure on plane

WARNING - DISTRESSING CONTENT: Niaomi Baker, 33, travelled to Tunisia but faced a medical emergency on the plane due to take her back home - the Brit remains in hospital more than two months on

View 5 Images Niaomi Baker in hospital abroad (Image: Laylla Baker / SWNS)

The family of a British woman stuck more than 1,000 miles away from home, after she collapsed on holiday, said they "feel helpless".

‌



Niaomi Baker, 33, was due to fly back to the UK from Tunisia when she suffered a seizure onboard the plane and was rushed to hospital - where she was placed in an induced coma. The 33-year-old, from Kirkby, Merseyside, has remained bedbound in the costal city of Sousse two months after she collapsed. Niaomi suffers from epilepsy, autism and functional neurological disorder (FND), and her family are battling to bring her home for treatment.

‌



Although doctors have since brought Niaomi out of the coma, the Brit has not regained full consciousness.

‌



View 5 Images Niaomi Baker before the medical emergency (Image: Laylla Baker / SWNS)

Niaomi's cousin Laylla Baker said the 33-year-old went abroad without the knowledge of her family - and without travel insurance despite her medical conditions. Laylla said: "It's hard to explain what we're going through as a family. You see things like this on the news but you don't expect it to happen to someone you know."

The cousin, who is also from Merseyside, said the family had no idea Niaomi left the country until she was told by one of her carers days after the plane incident. Laylla said she had concerns over why this happened, as she is her cousin's next of kin.

‌



View 5 Images The 33-year-old in a hospital bed (Image: Laylla Baker / SWNS)

She said: "I don't really know exactly what's happened and what date she went there. I didn't even know she was going on holiday. No one informed us."

The cousin said Niaomi fell ill as she boarded her return flight on February 11, adding: "Apparently, she was due to fly back home, but she suffered a medical episode and had a seizure on the plane.

‌



"They removed her from the aircraft and took her to the local hospital in Sousse where she carried on having seizures. They don't know anything about Niaomi's medical background, so they've obviously thought the best thing to do was to put her in an induced coma."

5 View 5 Images The woman remains in hospital more than two moths after the incident (Image: Laylla Baker / SWNS) 5 View 5 Images Niaomi's cousin said she suffers from several medical conditions (Image: Laylla Baker / SWNS)

‌



Niaomi has lived with epilepsy since the age of two and also has FND - a neurological condition that can cause seizures, weakness and difficulties with movement and communication. Laylla said her cousin has also suffered trauma, including the devastating loss of her mum Karen, who she found dead in bed two years ago.

Laylla shared her concerns for her cousin and said the situation has been made worse as she is unable to travel to Tunisia due to her own health concerns. She said: "She's out there on her own and I'm worried that the reason she's not coming round is because she's got no one to talk to her. It's just horrible."

The 34-year-old added: "I've got a brain tumour that I've been battling for six years. I can't fly there due to my medical condition. I just wish I was able to be there with her, because I think I'd be able to get her to come round. I really do believe that."

‌



Laylla also hit out at authorities, claiming her cousin had been "failed" after travelling abroad without family knowledge despite requiring daily care, saying: "Adult social care have failed her. She normally has carers going to visit her four times a day. That tells you everything you need to know.

"If you had any doubt in your head that Niaomi was not capable of doing this, why didn't you help her - or inform family members? I feel like she has been failed by the system really badly."

Communication with doctors abroad has also proved difficult, with Laylla relying on the British embassy for updates. She said: "It's an absolute nightmare. The hospital were in contact with us when she was intensive care. But she has been out there for nine weeks now and I've not heard anything from doctors a week."

Article continues below

The family are desperately trying to raise around £35,000 to fund a medical air ambulance to bring Niaomi back to the UK, where they hope she can be treated at the Walton Centre in Liverpool. Laylla said: "She's a UK citizen and a vulnerable adult stuck abroad." The fundraiser for Niaomi can be found here.

News.title: Former BNP leader Nick Griffin enters not guilty pleas in crown court appearance
News.content:
Former BNP leader Nick Griffin enters not guilty pleas in crown court appearance

Former BNP leader Nick Griffin, 67, has denied stirring up racial hatred with a cartoon during an appearance at Southwark Crown Court in south London today for a private prosecution

View 3 Images Former British National Party (BNP) leader Nick Griffin arrived for a hearing at Southwark Crown Court, south London (Image: PA)

Former BNP leader Nick Griffin appeared in a London crown court today and denied stirring up racial hatred with a cartoon shared on social media.

‌



The 67-year-old, who led the BNP from 1999 to 2014, is facing a private criminal prosecution brought by activists from the Campaign Against Antisemitism. At Southwark Crown Court Griffin formally entered not guilty pleas to two charges - displaying material likely to stir up racial hatred and publishing or distributing material likely to stir up racial hatred. Mr Justice Swift adjourned the case for a trial, which is set to begin on May 11 next year. Griffin, of Welshpool, Powys, is accused over a post on the social media platform X - formerly Twitter - featuring a cartoon of a giant spider with a Star of David on its head.

‌



View 3 Images Nick Griffin appeared at Southwark Crown Court (Image: PA)

‌



It is said he accompanied the allegedly antisemitic cartoon with a comment, in a post which was put on social media on December 6 2021. The post was "abusive or insulting", it is said, and Griffin is accused of "intending to stir up racial hatred".

Griffin sat behind his barrister for the day-long court hearing, and is set to return to court for the trial.Photographers pictured him arriving early at the crown court just outside London Bridge station. He smiled and appeared relaxed as he entered the court buildings.

‌



View 3 Images The hearing was at Southwark Crown Court (Image: BPM MEDIA)

Last year the Mirror reported how he wants so-called British nationalists to join the Army as reserves to receive military training ahead of a “civil war”.

He wrote: “My recommendation that patriotic young Brits should keep their political opinions to themselves and join the Army Reserve. That way, they get genuine military training perfectly legally, and are even paid while doing so.

Article continues below

“Those who have gone down this road will be a damned sight more use than those who got lured down the blind alley of illegality and thrown, still untrained, into prison. This is surely very much better than it would be to get involved in extremist fringe groups which indulge in very limited physical training.”

News.title: Greece scrambles fighter jets as 'Turkish planes with weapons invade airspace'
News.content:
Greece scrambles fighter jets as 'Turkish planes with weapons invade airspace'

Greece scrambled fighter jets in response to planes 'with weapons' from fellow NATO member Turkey infringing upon its airspace today, according to Greek media

View Image Greek media says fighter jets were scrambled in response to Turkish F-16s infringing upon its airspace today (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

A NATO member has been forced to scramble fighter jets after another member state's planes infringed upon its airspace, according to reports.

‌



Greek media reports the country deployed fighters to intercept Turkish F-16s and a single CN-235 naval cooperation aircraft.

‌



According to Eleftheros Typos, five aircraft from Turkey committed infringements of Greek airspace in the northeastern and southeastern Aegean today - four F-16 fighters, two of which were carrying weapons, as well as a single CN-235 naval cooperation aircraft.

‌



The local site reports that the Turkish aircraft were identified and intercepted "in accordance with international rules, as is standard practice". No engagements occurred.

Major UK car seller to shut down within days – more than 50 years in business READ MORE :

This comes after RAF fighter jets were scrambled yesterday in the UK over concerns of a suspected Russian bomber approaching the UK.

Two RAF Typhoons were deployed from RAF Lossiemouth in Scotland. A Voyager refuelling jet also took off from RAF Brize Norton in Oxfordshire. The planes flew towards Shetland.

‌



According to The Telegraph, an unidentified Russian warplane remained outside British airspace. The Typhoons later returned to their base as the Russian plane did not need to be intercepted. Sources told the publication that the deployment of British fighter jets tracking the Russian aircraft was part of a wider NATO response.

In recent weeks Russian warships and submarines have passed close to UK waters.

The UK and allies tracked a Russian attack submarine and two spy submarines loitering over critical undersea cables in the North Atlantic for a month before they retreated, John Healey revealed earlier this month.

‌



A British warship and aircraft were deployed to deter “malign” activity by Moscow in waters off the UK’s northern coast, the Defence Secretary said.

He said Vladimir Putin had sought to capitalise on the world being “distracted” by the Iran war and that he poses “the primary threat to UK security”.

Addressing the Russian president, Mr Healey said: “We see your activity over our cables and our pipelines, and you should know that any attempt to damage them will not be tolerated and will have serious consequences.”

Article continues below

Mr Healey told a press conference in Downing Street that in the past few weeks – while many eyes were trained on the Middle East crisis – the UK, in partnership with Norway and other allies, responded to “increased Russian activity” in the Atlantic north of the UK.

News.title: Hotels in US cities forced to slash World Cup prices because of lack of demand
News.content:
Hotels in US cities forced to slash World Cup prices because of lack of demand

Some hotels in US cities, such as Dallas, hosting World Cup games have cut prices by a third in the wake of lacklustre demand from fans deterred by high ticket costs for matches

View 3 Images Dallasis among the World Cup host cities where hoteliers have had to slash prices (Image: Art Wager)

Hotels in the US have begun slashing prices for this summer’s World Cup due to a lack of demand.

‌



Figures suggest room rates have been cut by around a third in cities hosting games for the tournament, including Dallas where England play their opening match against Croatia in June 19. It comes amid a reported backlash at high ticket prices for games and anti-US sentiment.

‌



Gianni Infantino, head of football governing body Fifa, had predicted the World Cup - being staged in the US, Canada and Mexico - would deliver a surge in guests for hoteliers.

‌



But Vijay Dandapani, president and chief executive of the Hotel Association of New York City, said he could “categorically say we haven’t seen much of a meaningful boost yet.

“It’s possible we will get some more demand, but at this point it certainly will not be the cornucopia that Fifa was promising,” he told the Financial Times.

Scott Yesner, founder of hotel management company Bespoke Stay, said: “I’m seeing a lot of people start to panic and lower their rates.”

‌



View 3 Images The boss of New York's hotel trade body said the promised boom in World Cup bookings has yet to be seen (Image: Getty Images)

England fans face sevenfold New York price increase in latest World Cup rip off READ MORE :

Pub bookings for World Cup already filling up fast - with two months left READ MORE :

Fifa itself has cancelled reservations for thousands of contracted hotel rooms for staff. While some over booking was expected, hoteliers say it has left them with a lot more rooms to sell.

Dates and UK times of home nations' group games

‌



England

England v Croatia - June 19 - 9pm - Dallas

England v Ghana - June 23 - 9pm - Boston

England v Panama - June 27 - 10pm - New York

‌



Scotland

Scotland v Haiti - June 14 - 2am - Boston

Scotland v Morocco - June 19 - 11pm - Boston

Scotland v Brazil - June 24 - 11pm - Miami

‌



Lior Sekler, chief commercial officer at hotel operator HRI Hospitality, blamed dissatisfaction with US President Donald Trump’s administration, along with visa and immigration policies, for deterring visitors. “Obviously, people’s desire to come to the United States is down right now,” he added.

View 3 Images England fans face shelling out up to £515 for tickets team's group games

Some fans are believed to be put off by sky high ticket prices for games.

Article continues below

The cheapest tickets cost 10 times the price promised in the original bid for the World Cup by the three countries. England fans will need to shell out at least $220 (£162) for the team’s group games against Ghana in Boston on June 23, and against Panama on June 27 in New York, rising to $700 (£515) for category one tickets for the opener against Croatia.

Prices then go up rapidly the further into the tournament teams get, with tickets to the final costing up to £6,400 each. The Football Supporters Association has labelled the prices “scandalous” .

News.title: Dark life of looksmaxxing influencer Clavicular from 'Hitler video' to suspected overdose
News.content:
Dark life of looksmaxxing influencer Clavicular from 'Hitler video' to suspected overdose

Clavicular, real name Braden Peters, is one of the internet's most controversial figures. Now, as fans fear for his wellbeing after a suspected overdose, we look at the dark world he found fame in...

View 5 Images The influencer has admitted himself that he's gone down a dark path (Image: clavicular0/Instagram )

In a dark corner of the internet where self-improvement blurs into extreme obsession, few figures are as controversial as Clavicular.

To his 760,000 TikTok followers, he was once the poster boy for "looksmaxxing" - a hyper-online subculture that promotes extreme and often dangerous methods of improving physical apearance.

Young men are being taught by figures like Clavicular - real name Braden Peters - that there are 'tools' at their disposal for severe self-optimisation. But it's not just exercise of face masks. Extreme steroid use, surgery and even taking a hammer to your jaw or cheekbones are all tactics promoted by looksmaxxers - to chisel their physique like Greek gods.

Clavicular hospitalised: Dark moment live stream cuts off after suspected overdose READ MORE :

The influencer has bragged about taking so much testosterone that he is now 'infertile', and once nearly cried when he discovered his burger had cheese on it as he was terrified of a cortisol spike.

After gaining looksmaxxing fame, Peters burst through the subculture into mainstream media when he cosied up to manopshere leader Andrew Tate. He also landed a modelling role at New York fashion week.

But his life appears to have taken a darker turn as the star was hospitalised this week after a suspected overdose. Here, we look at his biggest controversies...

View 5 Images Clavicular stormed out of the interview when questioned on Andrew Tate (Image: 60 Minutes)

Andrew Tate friendship

Peters first gained traction on platforms like TikTok, where he documented his physical transformation in obsessive detail.

Jawlines, posture, bone structure - nothing was too minor to analyse. His content tapped into a growing audience of young men drawn to the promise that attractiveness could be engineered through discipline and extreme routines.

But from early on, there were warning signs. The tone of his posts often veered into harsh, absolutist thinking, dividing people into categories and promoting a worldview that critics say overlaps with toxic online communities.

As his profile grew, Clavicular was linked to controversial online personalities, including those orbiting figures like Andrew Tate. In a heated 60 Minutes Australia interview, just days before his alleged overdose, he was questioned about his connection to the controversial figure.

Adam Hegarty asked the influencer: "You've shared company with Andrew Tate and other controversial figures, why do you spend time with people like that?", to which the influencer replied: "I see you want to make this political... You want to end [this interview] and talk about politics." He then got up and stormed out.

View 5 Images Part of his social media is 'coaching' men on how to be more handsome (Image: clavicular0/Instagram )

Hitler song

One of the most widely condemned moments in his online career came when a video circulated showing him singing a song referencing Adolf Hitler.

He was filmed with far-right commentator Nick Fuentes and Andrew Tate chanting along to Kanye West's song "Heil Hitler". The clip sparked immediate backlash. Viewers accused him of trivialising one of history's most horrific regimes, while others questioned whether the act was intended as shock humour or something more serious.

He never fully addressed the incident in a way that satisfied critics, and the controversy lingered.

Battery arrest

Away from the camera, Clavicular's personal life appeared no less turbulent. In February, he was arrested in Florida on suspicion of battery and taken into custody. The 20-year-old was accused of instigating a fight between his girlfriend and another 19-year-old woman in February at a Kissimmee short-term rental.

View 5 Images Braden Peters, AKA Clavicular, refers to women as 'targets' or 'foids' (Image: clavicular0/Instagram )

According to the sheriff's office, the influencer and his 24-year-old girlfriend Violet Marie Lentz are suspected of involvement in an attack on the woman. It was later alleged that he posted the violence on social media to exploit the two women.

In a separate incident, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission also announced it was launching an investigation into a video showing an alligator being shot at multiple times in the Florida Everglades.

The video shows four people, allegedly including Clavicular, on an airboat in the Everglades appearing to discharge firearms at an alligator.

‌



Spiralling live streams

Before the influencer's alleged overdose, followers noted increasingly erratic posts, abrupt shifts in mood and messaging, and a sense that the carefully curated image of control was beginning to fracture.

During a recent livestream, Clavicular appeared to be under the influence, according to some fans. Taking to X later, fellow influencer Androgenic had said: "I hadn't seen him in this state before and he went from speaking to being fairly unresponsive in mere seconds. Within a minute we all realised the situation, turned the stream off, picked him up and rushed him to the hospital."

A video later emerged of the streamer being carried to a black car as an ambulance arrived. It has been reported that Clavicular is now in a stable condition but remains in hospital.

‌



Extreme measures and coaching

In his life, Clavicular has made a string of bold claims about what he's done to change his looks to become more attractive to women and to gain power, including claimed he used meth to keep his weight down and had been injecting testosterone since the age of 14.

He now has more than 760,000 followers on TikTok, and charges men a fee for coaching them on how to become more handsome. It's thought he earns thousands from his online posts, particularly on Kick where he earned £74,000 in one month alone.

View 5 Images He started taking steroids at 14 (Image: clavicular0/Instagram )

‌



But his looks have come with a hefty price. He said he's infertile after years of steroid abuse after starting looksmaxxing at just 14-years-old. He ordered testosterone and fat dissolvers on the internet and used Photoshop to change his appearance.

In November, he shared himself seemingly injecting his then 17-year-old girlfriend with fat-dissolving peptides, calling himself "Dr Clav". The following month he seemed to strike a pedestrian with his Tesla Cybertruck, asking "Is he dead? Hopefully".

He claimed the man had been stalking him, but others said the incident was staged for views. He once described his own life as a "f***ing horror story", admitting he will never get to live a "normal life" again.

Article continues below

For emotional support you can call the Samaritans 24-hour helpline on 116 123, email jo@samaritans.org, visit a Samaritans branch in person or go to the Samaritans website.

News.title: Cash-strapped man, 81, tied up 95-year-old woman and tried to rob her, court hears
News.content:
Cash-strapped man, 81, tied up 95-year-old woman and tried to rob her, court hears

Retired pharmacy courier Edwin Morrison, who strangled the woman shouting: “Give me your money” before zip-tying her hands, has now been jailed for seven years after a court hearing

CCTV of Edwin Morrison who robbed 95-year-old woman in Little Hulton

A cash-strapped pensioner who robbed a 95-year-old woman in her own home to help pay for his funeral has been jailed for seven years.

‌



Retired pharmacy courier Edwin Morrison, 81, knocked on the woman’s door telling her he wanted to discuss the new bin collection date. Without invitation, he then stepped inside under the guise of discussing things further.

‌



Once inside, the woman sat on her armchair, sat on her footrest, took off his gloves, and put his hand around her throat. As he strangled her, he repeatedly asked for the woman’s money and purse - shouting: “Give me your money”.

‌



View 2 Images Scene where Edwin Morrison forced his way into 95-year-old's house (Image: ITV News)

Morrison then proceeded to zip-tie her hands together, before again grabbing and squeezing her throat. His victim pleaded with him to let her go as she said she could not breathe, but Morrison told her to “shut up”.

Morrison fled empty-handed from the property in Little Hulton, Salford, as he was foiled by the arrival of the woman’s mobile hairdresser, Manchester Crown Court heard.

‌



At a previous hearing, Morrison was said to have attempted to rob the woman as a way to pay for his funeral. However, at his sentencing today (Weds) the court heard he was hoping to use the money to buy his partner a new kitchen before taking his own life.

On New Year’s Day, he had set up an online GoFundMe appeal titled “Help to bury me” as he outlined his health problems. It raised nothing. He wrote: “More or less been told to go in a corner and see my time out. I have no money to cover funeral costs and other incidentals.”

He targeted his vulnerable victim after he visited her home previously when delivering medication as part of his former job. Morrison, who has no previous convictions, retired aged 75 and was diagnosed with terminal kidney cancer in May 2024, the court heard. Prosecutors said he was regularly gambling at his local bookmaker’s in the months before the attack on 27 January 2026.

‌



The court was told a psychiatric report had concluded Morrison was suffering from a “depressive disorder” by the end of 2025. In a combination of “depression and despair:”, he is said to have decided to end his life in February, while his partner was away on a break. Morrison did not want to be a financial burden to his family in paying for his funeral, said his barrister Nick Clarke.

View 2 Images Morrison had set up a GoFundMe appeal to pay for his funeral (Image: eyJpdiI6IlJkbW1oKzNjU3lzY0VKaWpNM1BXNUE9PSIsInZhbHVlIjoia01zekd4SjcycE1Dek1TNVlVZ3g2WnhvQ0pacUF5c0JOcmpDOWF6UUluRFAzcC9wZllvVFp0QWx5WHlXOTgwN0Jaa3Mvb3RDWkVmcTZ2Uzk1QVBVNXc9PSIsIm1hYyI6IjZmN2I4OTdhM2Fh)

Mr Clarke told the court: “The GoFundMe page was unsuccessful…so he came up with this particular scheme, which in his mind would not be complicated and not cause the problems that it did.

‌



“He was utterly selfish and self-centred – for perhaps the first time in his life – in committing this offence. He is remorseful for what he has done. It is submitted that no real harm was intended. The motivation for this offending was altruistic rather than malicious.”

In a victim impact statement, his victim told the court: “I thought I was going to die.” Shortly after, mobile hairdresser Michaela Nelson arrived for her weekly appointment and let herself in.

Mr Smith said: “Ms Nelson went into the lounge and saw an old man sitting in front of the victim and assumed he was a friend. (The victim) shouted at her to call the police and she at first thought it was a joke.”

‌



Morrison then held his hands up as if he was going to grab the throat of the hairdresser, the court was told, before she ran away and he left the house. Police arrived shortly after and Morrison was traced to his home address by the movements of his Peugeot, the court heard.

In March, he pleaded guilty to a single count of attempted robbery. The prosecution asked for other alleged offences of false imprisonment and intentional strangulation to lie on file.

Detective Inspector Paul Davies, from GMP’s Salford district, said: “When this job first came in, we were all shocked by the very nature of it, and we immediately launched a full investigation into the circumstances.

Article continues below

“It was a terrifying ordeal for the victim and Morrison’s actions of targeting a woman in her own home were shocking. Her resilience and strength following this vile crime have been truly inspirational and I am glad that the investigative team have been able to get her the justice she deserves.

“I also want to commend the brave actions of her hairdresser who arrived as the crime was happening. She prevented Morrison from doing anything further, got him out of the living room, and called 999 straight away.

“This investigation has seen countless of hours of work, from initial response to CCTV checks to door-to-door enquiries – from the start, the entire team have done their utmost best which has seen Morrison put behind bars today.”

News.title: Man, 21, rejected three times from binman job after nine-month unpaid internship
News.content:
Man, 21, rejected three times from binman job after nine-month unpaid internship

Bryan Rowe completed a nine-month unpaid internship with Southampton City Council but was rejected three times for a job as a binman — his mum slammed the decision as "cruel and unfair"

View 2 Images Bryan Rowe was rejected from a binman job three times (Image: Family/Solent News)

A young man said he was rejected for a binman job with the council three times despite completing a nine-month unpaid internship, with him mum it was an "unfair kick in the teeth".

‌



Bryan Rowe, 21, said he was rejected twice by Southampton City Council but it claimed the man had initially been rejected in error. The aspiring binman was then called in for an interview but Mr Rowe was turned away from the job again. The 21-year-old had worked unpaid at the council between November 2024 and June 2025, as part of a supported internship.

‌



Mr Rowe has ADHD and myotonic dystrophy — a form of muscular dystrophy that impacts muscles and other organs — and had been a lorry loader during his unpaid internship. The 21-year-old said he was encouraged to apply for vacancies once his internship was over but has been rejected multiple times.

‌



View 2 Images Bryan Rowe (right) with his mum Claire Rowe (left) (Image: Family/Solent News)

Man missed red flags and lost his job to AI twice in 40 days READ MORE :

When he was rejected the second time, the council emailed him claiming an error led to people being sent incorrect information. The young man was "always enthusiastic" and did well during his nine-month internship, and wanted to be a binman since he was a young kid.

After his third rejection, the 21-year-old's mum, Claire Rowe, slammed the decision as "cruel and unfair". The mum argued the council should have just said no to her son and "let it drop" if they thought he was not right for the job.

‌



Ms Rowe said: "You were better off saying no and letting us be done with it, now they've kicked him back in the teeth again. I find that hard to take as his mother that has spent the weekend trying to explain to him that he is good enough and that someone one day is going to want him.

"I just think it's cruel and unfair. He wants to get out there as a disabled person and work and get some confidence, some money of his own." She added: "It's very, very disappointing. He is devastated, it's absolutely awful. I just cannot believe that this has happened again."

A spokesperson for Southampton City Council told the Mirror: "We received a high volume of applications for the advertised role; however, we cannot comment on individual applications or candidates. All the applications and interviews have followed the council's recruitment process. We wish all of the unsuccessful candidates well in their future endeavours."

Article continues below

Mr Rowe, after the first two rejections, said: "I felt very disappointed not to get the job after two interviews with the council I worked for, I told mum that I am not good enough to get anything not even a binman job."

The mum added: "He worked for free for nine months, he was always enthusiastic and on time. How are people meant to get enough experience?"

Ms Rowe said she raised a formal complaint with Southampton City Council and was told the council was reviewing its recruitment services.

News.title: Social media ban for U16s isn't the power move you think it is without this major change
News.content:
Social media ban for U16s isn't the power move you think it is without this major change

As countries across the globe consider a social media ban for their under-16 citizens, I'd argue that a blanket ban is counterproductive without one major change that could keep kids offline for good

View 2 Images The UK government has since launched a consultation on banning social media for under-16s

Countries around the world are considering following in Australia’s footsteps by trialling a social media ban for under-16s. The ban came into place for Australian teenagers in December and platforms like TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, Snapchat, and X must take "reasonable steps" to restrict access or face a fine.

‌



The UK government has since launched a consultation on banning social media for under-16s, while Denmark, Greece, Spain and Ireland have considered similar bans: Spain and Ireland for under-16s, Denmark and Greece for under-15s and Austria for under-14s.

‌



Greece’s social media ban for under-15s will come into place on January 1, 2027, with Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis stating that “long hours in front of screens does not allow their minds to rest”.

‌



Meanwhile, the UK government is set to trial the ban alongside its consultation. The test will see 300 teens have their social apps disabled entirely, blocked overnight or capped to one hour's use. According to the BBC, Technology Secretary Liz Kendall said it was about "testing different options in the real world", and hopes the pilots will help to inform whether an Australian-style ban would work for UK teens.

View 2 Images Greece’s social media ban for under-15s will come into place on January 1, 2027 (Image: 2026 Anna Barclay)

Lauren Cowell on the heartbreaking reason she wants social media law change READ MORE :

Dad of teen who took own life issues plea amid Australia social media ban fears READ MORE :

Experts have opposed the ban, with many calling it a “lazy fix” that creates “a false sense of safety that quickly unravels”, and instead urging governments to reduce the “financial incentive for social media companies to target and addict kids.”

‌



With that being said, I’m against a blanket ban on social media for under-16s as it fails to address a root cause that can no longer be overlooked.

Having watched social media grow into the behemoth it is today – and how its addictive nature has cost the lives of young people around the world – I’d strongly advocate for the removal of addictive designs, like infinite scrolling, and reinstating features like the "you're all caught up" notifications from the early days of Instagram. Current measures like TikTok’s daily timers are, in my opinion, largely performative (a four digit code is all that stops me from bypassing my doomscroll).

Instead, the UK should ensure they're able to answer one key question: what replaces social media for teens if a ban is introduced, as spaces for young people to ‘hang out' are rapidly declining?

‌



I grew up without smartphones and social media, then saw it come in during my teens - it didn’t just pull people in, it arrived as everything else was quietly disappearing. Youth clubs, community spaces, cheap places lost funding and closed, leaving nowhere for us teenagers to actually go.

I remember a Friday youth club my whole friendship group attended in the early 2000s – £2 entry, games, a tuck shop. It gave us somewhere to be and something everyone did together. Then it closed due to lack of funding and nothing replaced it. We were left to our own devices, literally, and resorted to meeting up online, via chatrooms and video calling apps like ooVoo and Skype.

Around the UK, spending on youth services by local authorities has dropped by 73% over the last decade. By 2023, about 1,200 publicly run youth centres had closed, and more than 4,500 youth workers had lost their jobs, according to The Guardian.

‌



Since then, the Labour government has committed to reopening youth clubs, starting with the first eight ‘Young Futures Hubs’ which are set to open in Birmingham, Brighton and Hove, Bristol, County Durham, Leeds, Manchester, Nottingham, and Tower Hamlets under the government’s National Youth Strategy.

As Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy pointed out, "the closure of over a thousand youth centres since 2010 didn’t just take away facilities, it took away community, connection and opportunity for a generation. We are determined to rebuild that."

But it’s not just historical – two major activity hubs for young people, North London’s Finchley Lido and Rowans in Finsbury Park are currently under threat from developers, so this is still playing out.

‌



Without more physical third spaces - and adequate investment to keep them running – you leave under-16s with nothing to do. These are formative years that shouldn't be spent glued to screens, but where do these kids go instead?

I used to read teen magazines like Sugarscape and Teen Vogue, I’d browse through glitter eyeshadows and pastel-coloured bracelets in Claire’s or buy a new game for my Nintendo in GAME. This year, Claires, “the hottest store on the high street” for any 14 year old, went into administration. GAME suffered a similar fate despite gaming being most popular among Gen Alpha. SugarScape no longer exists and Teen Vogue laid off its staff to fold under its parent publication, Vogue.

The market for teenagers has disappeared, swallowed up by 'young adulthood'. Kids are often in the same spaces as people twice their age. I find myself shopping in Sephora alongside 13 year olds stocking up on Drunk Elephant and, I can’t blame them – there’s no in-between anymore.

‌



With so few spaces designed just for young people, they’re being pushed into adult environments earlier, blurring the boundaries between adulthood and youth altogether. Those few spaces that are catered to teens – take GoApe (up to £44 per person) or Gravity in Bluewater (up to £35 per person) for example – aren’t pocket-money cheap, placing yet another financial burden on parents.

In theory, reducing screen time for teens makes sense, but for a social media ban for under-16s to actually work, the UK needs to ensure there’s something for teens to do in the interim, something that is well funded, affordable, accessible and encourages simply “hanging out”. Until these physical third spaces are in place, removing the only space for teens to enjoy themselves - albeit virtual - is counterproductive.

Using Australia as the example doesn't check out, either. This is where a ban has already been tried – and the results aren’t promising. Platforms like Instagram, Snapchat and YouTube say nearly five million accounts have been blocked in Australia since the ban began but also claim accurate age determination is challenging.

‌



Some teens are reportedly shifting to smaller, alternative messaging and image- and video-sharing apps such as Lemon8 or Coverstar, which has been dubbed a "cool app we can all move to."

Over on Reddit, parents and guardians shared how kids have “worked their way around” the ban, with one writing: “My kid put on makeup and made a new account and it didn’t get flagged. I'm not sure about others but I’d say kids have worked around it.”

Another added: “All the kids I coach just started new accounts. Nothing changed as far as I know.”

Article continues below

A report by the child safety campaign group the Molly Rose Foundation found that four months after Australia’s ban came into force, about 60% of 12-15 year-olds who had accounts on restricted platforms still have access to one or more of them, and on top of that, many don’t feel any safer.

Young people are lonely and phone-addicted, but they’re yearning for community. So before we ban phones or social media, let's make sure we're actually giving them a reason to get off their phones.

News.title: British doubles legend Jamie Murray retires from tennis
News.content:
Murray will be remembered for his razor-sharp volleying skills and the preposterous angles he conjured at the net. His returns were often unorthodox and he was fond of a lobbed service return to unsettle opponents.

Looking back at his achievements, Murray said he was proud to have represented his hometown of Dunblane and the country of Scotland at the highest level.

"There is no history of tennis and no environment of tennis [in Scotland]," Murray told BBC Sport.

"I'd imagine the odds were against us from the start but we were able to make some good things happen."

His mother Judy thought Jamie had the better hand-eye co-ordination of her sons when young. Jamie and Andy briefly became rivals as tennis players - and also while wrestling.

Judy once recalled: "Andy's favourite [wrestler] was The Rock and Jamie's was Stone Cold Steve Austin, and they used to create these bouts that they saw on the television. They used to wrestle each other on the duvet and thump each other with pillows, and create these belts and make up their own rules and scoring systems."

Jamie is 15 months older than Andy, and as his early dominance on the tennis court started to fade Andy says he quite literally bore the brunt.

"We were coming back from Solihull in the minibus and I'd beaten Jamie in the final, I think, of the under-12s, so basically I was winding him up about that and my hand was on the hand rest," he told BBC Sport in 2015.

"We were sitting next to each other and he just basically punched me on the hand - I lost my fingernail and I've still got the scars to show for it."

Despite some defeats against his brother, Jamie was still very much on track for a professional singles career until a negative experience at an LTA training school in Cambridge in his very early teens.

He struggled with living away from home and the elite training environment, and even though he has never sought to blame the LTA, his forehand suffered and he has said he was never quite the same player again.

News.content:

Tom Homan, the man charged with masterminding President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown, has called on Pope Leo XIV to “just stay out” of political matters.

“Look, I’m not gonna speak for the president,” Homan told reporters gathered outside the White House Tuesday. “I’m speaking for myself, a lifelong Catholic. I wish they would stay out of immigration if they don’t know what they’re talking about.”

open image in gallery Tom Homan has become the latest member of the Trump administration to order Pope Leo XIV to stay out of politics ( AFP/Getty )

“If they wore my shoes for 40 years and talked to a nine-year-old little girl that got raped multiple times, or stood in the back of a trailer, 19 dead aliens at my feet, including a five-year-old boy that baked to death, if they understood the atrocities that happened on open border, I think they, their opinion would change,” Homan continued.

He went on to say that, while he welcomed discussion, “illegal immigration is not a victimless crime,” praising Trump for “saving thousands of lives a year because he has a secure border.”

“Human traffickers are out of business, right?” he said. “The cartels are going bankrupt because of that secure border. I wish that they’d understand that, because if they did, I think they would have a different opinion.”

Later, Homan was interviewed by Rob Schmitt on Newsmax and repeated his objections to the church speaking out.

“It’s unacceptable, and I’ve called the Pope out before,” he told Schmitt. “I’m a lifelong Catholic. Baptized, first communion, confirmation.

open image in gallery Homan resumes his attack on the Pope in conversation with Rob Schmitt on Newsmax ( Newsmax )

“Look, I’ve spent my whole life in the Catholic Church, but I’m disappointed that they want to weigh in on political issues like this. There are enough problems with the Catholic Church – and I know because I’m a member of the Catholic Church – that they need to fix and concentrate on and leave politics alone.

“I mean, they talk about that they don’t believe in a secure border, they need to support open borders. However, if you cross the wall at the Vatican, you’re going to prison, and the penalties are much worse there than they are here.”

He continued: “I wish they would sit down and let me educate them on open borders. When President Trump has illegal immigration down 97 percent, how many women aren’t being raped by the cartels? How many children aren’t dying making that journey? How many pounds of fentanyl aren’t killing Americans? How many women and children aren’t being sex trafficked?

“I wish they would sit down. We want to sit down with them and explain why a secure border is a safer border and a secure border gives us stronger national security.

“I think they’re talking from a position of not knowing what I know, what happens behind the scenes on illegal immigration. I’d be willing to sit down with them. I’m disappointed they’re taking this position.”

open image in gallery Pope Leo XIV has been completely unmoved by the Trump administration's fury over his criticism of the Iran war ( Reuters )

The feud between the two camps erupted when the Pope gave a service at St Peter’s Basilica Saturday at which he said prayers for peace serve as “a bulwark against that delusion of omnipotence that surrounds us and is becoming increasingly unpredictable and aggressive.”

Addressing warmongering leaders, without naming names, he said: “To them we cry out: stop! It is time for peace! Sit at the table of dialogue and mediation – not at the table where rearmament is planned and deadly actions are decided.

“Enough of the idolatry of self and money! Enough of the display of power! Enough of war! True strength is shown in serving life.”

Trump took the comments personally and retaliated by calling the pontiff “WEAK on Crime, and terrible for Foreign Policy” and then posting a blasphemous meme of himself as Christ, an astonishing episode that risked further offending his own Christian base a week on from his foul-mouthed tirade against Iran on Easter Sunday.

While the Pope himself brushed aside the insult, Vice President JD Vance, a convert to Catholicism, was forced to defend Trump, saying the meme had been “a joke” and, like Homan, urging His Holiness to “stick to matters of morality… and let the president of the United States stick to dictating American public policy.”

Italian PM Giorgia Meloni has meanwhile defended the Pope, saying: “Frankly, I would not feel at ease in a society where religious leaders do what political leaders tell them to do.”
